home.title: CashPilot: every earner, every box, one view
home.description: Free, open-source software that runs bandwidth sharing, DePIN, mining, GPU and storage services on your own machines, keeps them off your home network by default, and shows every payout in one dashboard.

hero.title: Put your idle hardware to work. See every payout in one dashboard.
hero.lead: CashPilot sets up bandwidth sharing, DePIN, mining, GPU and storage services on your computers, home servers and Raspberry Pi. On a new Docker install, the services it starts cannot reach your LAN, your router or the machine they run on. It reads your balance from each provider and keeps the history in one place, on your own machine.
hero.expect: CashPilot does not pay you. The providers do. Earnings depend on your country, connection and hardware.
hero.imageAlt: The CashPilot dashboard: the balance, the earnings today and this month, the services on each machine, and the earnings per day.
hero.imageAltMobile: The CashPilot dashboard on a phone: the balance, and the earnings today and this month.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: Three steps, and no account with us.

install.title: Install CashPilot
install.text: Use the desktop app on one computer. Or run the server with Docker on a home server, NAS or Raspberry Pi.

pick.title: Pick your services
pick.text: Choose from the catalog, sign up with the provider and paste your login. For services with a Docker image, CashPilot starts it in its own container. For the others it reads your balance.

watch.title: Watch every payout
watch.text: CashPilot reads your balances every hour and keeps the history. When a balance drops, it asks you whether you were paid.

bandwidth.text: Share the internet bandwidth you do not use with data and proxy companies.

depin.name: DePIN
depin.text: Run nodes for decentralised networks that pay in tokens.

compute.name: GPU compute
compute.text: Rent out your graphics card for AI and rendering jobs.

storage.name: Storage
storage.text: Rent out spare disk space to storage networks.

catch.title: What's the catch?
catch.lead: A fair question. Here are the facts.

free.title: Free
free.text: No price, no paid plan and no ads.

open.title: Open source
open.text: GPL-3.0. You can read every line on GitHub.

hardware.title: Runs on your hardware
hardware.text: Your machines and your connection. We run no servers for you.

account.title: No account with us
account.text: No sign-up and no email. You sign up only with the providers you choose.

catch.funding: How is it paid for? Some provider links are referral links. If you sign up through one, the provider may pay the CashPilot project a reward. It does not come out of your earnings.

control.title: You stay in control
control.lead: CashPilot runs on your machines. You can see what it does and stop it at any time.

logins.title: Your logins stay on your machine
logins.text: CashPilot stores them encrypted in its own database. Each login goes only to the service that needs it.

containers.title: Each service in its own container
containers.text: Every service CashPilot starts runs apart from the others, with its extra rights dropped and a limit on its processes.

lan.title: Kept off your home network
lan.text: On a new Docker install, the services it starts cannot reach your LAN, your router or the machine they run on. Protecting your home network.

stop.title: Stop anything at any time
stop.text: One click stops or removes a service. A guide shows how to remove CashPilot completely.

control.ratings: Every provider gets a grade from A to F on the same ten questions, and each answer links to its source.

earnings.title: What changes your earnings
earnings.lead: Nobody can promise you a figure. These are the things that move it.

country.title: Your country
country.text: Providers pay more for traffic from some countries than from others.

ip.title: Your type of IP address
ip.text: Many services pay only home connections, not servers in a data centre.

connection.title: Your connection
connection.text: More upload speed and no data cap leave room for more traffic.

uptime.title: Uptime
uptime.text: A device that stays on earns more than one that sleeps.

devices.title: Number of devices
devices.text: Most services allow one device per IP address and a set number per account.

hardware.title: Your GPU and hardware
hardware.text: GPU compute and mining depend on your card, your electricity price and the market.

earnings.note: Some setups earn very little. The dashboard shows what you really earn, so you can drop what does not pay.

compare.security: Security comes first in CashPilot. Every app it starts runs locked down and, by default, cannot reach your home network. Read the security defaults.

slow.q: Will it slow down my internet?
slow.a: It can. Bandwidth services send other companies' traffic through your connection, so they use some of your upload and download. CashPilot shows the network use of each machine, so you can see what uses the most and stop it.

legal.a: It depends on where you live and on your internet contract. Some internet providers forbid sharing or reselling your connection. Check your local law and your provider's terms before you start. This is not legal advice.

safe.a: Bandwidth services let other people's traffic use your IP address, so read each provider's terms first. CashPilot runs each service it starts in its own container and, on a new Docker install, keeps it off your home network. Read Protecting your home network before you start.

earn.a: We cannot tell you. It depends on your country, your type of IP address, your connection, your uptime and the services you run. Some setups earn very little. The dashboard shows what you really earn.

free.a: CashPilot is free software under the GPL-3.0 licence, built by its contributors. Some provider links are referral links, and the rewards from them help fund the project. How referrals work.

docker.a: Yes, for the services CashPilot starts, because they run in containers. The desktop app works with Docker or Podman, and its setup wizard helps you install Docker. The Android app does not need Docker, but it reports to a CashPilot server or desktop app.

pi.q: Does it run on a Raspberry Pi?
pi.a: Yes, on a Pi 3, 4 or 5 with the 64-bit system. Most services publish a build for ARM, and CashPilot checks before a deploy whether a service runs on your CPU. Running on ARM.

data.q: Does the CashPilot project see my logins or earnings?
data.a: No. CashPilot runs on your machines and sends nothing to the project. Your logins stay in your own CashPilot, encrypted in its database. Privacy.

cta.title: Ready to try it?
cta.text: Get the desktop app, or run the server with Docker. Both are free.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: What the CashPilot website and apps collect: the website collects nothing, and the apps send nothing to the project.
privacy.lead: Short version: this website collects nothing, and the CashPilot apps send nothing to the project.

site.title: This website
site.p1: No cookies, no analytics, no tracking pixels and no ads. The page loads nothing from other websites. The fonts are part of the site.
site.p2: When you pick a language, your browser keeps that choice in its local storage. It stays on your device and is never sent to us.
site.p3: GitHub Pages hosts this site, and Cloudflare carries the traffic to it. Both may log the IP address of each visit for security, and Cloudflare may ask your browser to report network errors to it. Read the GitHub privacy statement and the Cloudflare privacy policy.

apps.title: The CashPilot apps
apps.p1: The web server, the desktop app and the Android app have no telemetry. They send nothing to the CashPilot project.
apps.p2: Your logins and earnings stay in your own CashPilot. The apps connect only to the services they need: the providers you set up, GitHub to check for a new version, public IP and exchange-rate services, and blockchain explorers for on-chain balances.
apps.p3: Today the web dashboard also loads its fonts from Google Fonts and its chart library from jsDelivr. The docs list every outbound call and how to turn off the optional ones.

providers.title: Providers
providers.p1: When you sign up with a provider, that provider's own privacy policy applies. A referral link tells the provider that you came from CashPilot.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.description: CashPilot gives no financial or legal advice, promises no earnings, and is not part of the providers it runs.
disclaimer.lead: Please read this before you start.

advice.title: No financial or legal advice
advice.text: Nothing on this site or in the apps is financial, legal or tax advice.

earnings.title: No promised earnings
earnings.text: Earnings depend on your country, connection, hardware and the providers. They can be very small or zero. Providers can change their rates at any time.

law.title: Your law and your contract
law.text: Check your local law and your internet provider's terms before you share your connection or run a node. You are responsible for any taxes on what you earn.

providers.title: Independent providers
providers.text: The providers are separate companies. CashPilot is not part of them and cannot control their terms, payouts or account decisions. Some providers pay the project referral rewards.

warranty.title: No warranty
warranty.text: CashPilot is free software under the GPL-3.0-or-later licence. It comes without any warranty, as sections 15 and 16 of the licence say.

trademarks.title: Trademarks
